about: Research sheet for the Maryland county edition. Every contact below was read on the date in reviewed_on from the page named beside it; scripts/make_county_state.py turns it into the edition files.
name: Maryland
phones_sentence: Service office phones, addresses and hours come from the Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families office list. Offices are open by appointment only; call before you go.

offices.source_title: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families: How To Apply For Benefits (service offices)
offices.note: Department benefits specialists can help with VA claims, pension and survivor benefits. Offices are open by appointment only; call the office first.
offices.selection: Office address, phone and hours as printed on the department’s service office list. The list prints no county coverage, so each county shows a department office located in it; counties without one show the statewide service line and the nearest listed offices, as described in docs/MARYLAND.md. Staff names and emails omitted.

programs.name: Maryland veterans: accredited claims help
programs.organization: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families, Service and Benefits Program
programs.description: Free help from VA-accredited benefits specialists with VA claims, applications and appeals for veterans, dependents and survivors.
programs.next_step: Choose your county for its service office, or call the statewide service line at 800-446-4926 ext. 6450. Offices are by appointment only.
constraints: Offices are open Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m., by appointment only; call the office first.

sources.scope: Service centers with addresses and phones, and the statewide line 800-446-4926 ext. 6450; read in full.

programs.name: Maryland Access Point (Aging and Disability Resource Center)
programs.description: Maryland’s statewide entry point to long-term services and supports for older adults and people with disabilities: information, referral and options counseling through local Maryland Access Point offices, led mainly by Area Agencies on Aging with Centers for Independent Living. Military service is not required.
programs.next_step: Call 1-844-627-5465 (1-844-MAP-LINK) or dial 211 and ask for Maryland Access Point. Choose a county above for the direct number of its Area Agency on Aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

programs.name: Medicare counseling (SHIP) for Maryland
programs.organization: Maryland Department of Aging, Senior Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP)
programs.description: Free Medicare counseling from the Senior Health Insurance Assistance Program. Each Area Agency on Aging has a SHIP coordinator and trained volunteers who help with plan enrollment and Extra Help applications.
programs.next_step: Call 800-243-3425 and ask for Medicare counseling (SHIP), or ask your Area Agency on Aging for its SHIP counselor.
constraints: The state’s SHIP page is undated; the toll-free number on it matches the Department of Aging’s current contact page.

programs.name: Maryland Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program
programs.organization: Office of the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman, Maryland Department of Aging
programs.description: Statewide advocacy for residents of nursing homes and assisted living, delivered through the State office and 19 local ombudsman programs located at Area Agencies on Aging.
programs.next_step: Choose your county for its local ombudsman, or call the Maryland Department of Aging at 800-243-3425 and ask for the ombudsman program. To report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation of an adult, call Adult Protective Services at 800-332-6347. For immediate danger, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing or enforcement agency.

programs.name: Maryland Legal Aid
programs.description: Free civil legal help for people with low income, including a statewide telephone hotline for low-income veterans. Not criminal defense.
programs.next_step: Call central intake at 888-465-2468 and say if you are a veteran. Veterans can also call the Joining Forces hotline at 443-863-4040.
constraints: Applicants are screened; income, case type and capacity limits apply. Criminal, personal injury and traffic matters are not accepted.
The Joining Forces hotline hours listed in a bar-association directory are Tuesdays 3:00–7:00 p.m. and Thursdays 9:30 a.m.–1:30 p.m.; hours can change.

programs.name: VA medical centers serving Maryland
programs.description: VA Maryland Health Care System: Baltimore VA Medical Center (410-605-7000), Perry Point VA Medical Center (410-642-2411) and the Loch Raven campus. The state department lists the Washington DC VA Medical Center (202-745-8000) for Montgomery and Prince George’s Counties and Southern Maryland, and the Martinsburg VA Medical Center in West Virginia (304-263-0811) for Western Maryland. Community clinics are listed in VA’s facility locator.
programs.next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic and its medical center. Not enrolled yet? Ask a benefits specialist at your service office for help applying.
constraints: The state’s page names regions rather than counties, so this card does not assign counties. Your VA care team may be at a different clinic or system; follow what VA tells you.

coverage_scope: Referral edition. All 24 jurisdictions have a state benefits contact, a matched Area Agency on Aging and a local long-term-care ombudsman. The state’s office list prints no county coverage: 16 jurisdictions show an office located there and 8 show the statewide service line with nearby offices.
coverage_note: Service office addresses, phones and hours come from the Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families office list, which prints no county coverage; each county shows an office located in it, and counties without one show the statewide service line and nearby offices. Area Agencies on Aging come from the Department of Aging directory. Local ombudsman phones come from search excerpts of the Department of Aging ombudsman page. Centers for Independent Living come from the ILRU directory and the state’s 2024 directory. Reviewed November 15, 2026. Contacts are not telephone-confirmed.
